chunks: The man said, “She gifted her to me,” but the woman denied it. So he said: “You must bring me witnesses for that, or I will surely stone you with stones.” When the woman saw that, she confessed, and so ʿAlī عليه السلام administered the prescribed hadd punishment to her.

As for what the report contains in his statement, “He is not to be stoned if he commits zina with a Jewish woman, a Christian woman, or a slave-woman,” it is possible that this applies when he is not muhsan; because once ihsan is established, there is no difference whether his zina is with a Jewish woman, a Christian woman, a free woman, or a slave-woman, in whatever manner it may be. The apparent meaning of the Qur'an that we mentioned indicates this, as do the reports in applying the designation to him that he is a fornicator; and whatever indicates the obligation of stoning in one case indicates it in this case as well.
This is also reinforced by what he narrated:
Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā, from Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Mughīrah, from Ismāʿīl ibn Abī Ziyād, from Jaʿfar, from his father, from his forefathers عليهم السلام:

“Muḥammad ibn Abī Bakr wrote to ʿAlī عليه السلام asking him about a man who commits zina with a Jewish woman or a Christian woman. So he عليه السلام wrote back to him: ‘If he is muhsan, then stone him; and if he is a virgin, then flog him one hundred lashes, then banish him. As for the Jewish woman, send her to the people of her religion so that they may judge concerning her as they wish.’”

key_terms.اَلنَّصْرَانِيَّةِ: a Christian woman involved in the legal case
key_terms.اَلْيَهُودِيَّةِ: a Jewish woman involved in the legal case
key_terms.بِكْرًا: unmarried, for whom flogging applies here
key_terms.مُحْصَنًا: legally protected through marriage, making stoning applicable in zina cases
key_terms.يُرْجَمُ: is stoned as a hadd penalty

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on a Muslim man committing zina with a Jewish or Christian woman according to Imam ʿAlī عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This passage discusses legal rulings concerning zina, including the evidentiary demand in a specific case and the distinction between the muhsan and non-muhsan offender. It further cites a narration from Imam ʿAlī عليه السلام establishing that the hadd on the Muslim man depends on his marital status, even when the woman is Jewish or Christian.
